name: Ideal Time's buff is spent on one ability, not two (#3662)
contract: Ideal Time 807036 is a permanent passive (DurationIndex 21) whose two SPELL_AURA_PERIODIC_TRIGGER_SPELL effects fire every 30000 ms, one of them on 807210. 807210's Description and AuraDescription both read "Your next ability is guaranteed to critically strike", and Spell.dbc gives it DurationIndex 1 = 10000 ms, ProcFlags 0, ProcCharges 0 and ProcChance 100. Its effect 0 is Aura=290 SPELL_AURA_MOD_CRIT_PCT with EffectBasePoints 99 / EffectDieSides 1, a flat +100 that Player::UpdateWeaponDependentCritAuras sums into RANGED_CRIT_PERCENTAGE with no weapon requirement, which is where Unit::SpellDoneCritChance reads the chance for a DmgClass 3 spell. The tooltip therefore promises exactly two things: while the buff is up the next ability is a certain critical strike, and after that ability the promise is over - a second ability must be back to the player's ordinary chance. Shatter Echo 804503 is the ability because Spell.dbc gives it DmgClass 3 and family 28 word2 0x10, it carries CasterAuraSpell 804455 (Echo Fragment, fixtured with set_aura) and ranged_hit_rating removes any chance of a miss. Nothing here is probabilistic: the critical strike and the consumption are both pinned at 100%, so one cast settles it.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
Without the buff Shatter Echo is not a guaranteed critical strike
Ideal Time's buff as its 30-second periodic grant would leave it
Ideal Time's buff is present before the ability
Ideal Time's buff carries exactly one charge
The buff really does guarantee the next ability's critical strike
Echo Fragments satisfy Shatter Echo's CasterAuraSpell
Spend the buff on one ability
One ability ends Ideal Time's buff
A second ability is no longer a guaranteed critical strike
